cri_definition: CRI = 0.5 x pooled percentile(SAIDI) + 0.5 x pooled percentile(SAIFI), pooled over all 2013-2025 county-years; 0 = most reliable, 100 = least reliable. SAIDI/SAIFI include major event days; customer-weighted county allocation of utility-level EIA Form 861 data.
method: Projected CRI = county recent level (mean of last 5 observed years) + national within-county trend x (year - mid-year of those 5 years). Selected by rolling-origin backtest (origins 2016-2024, 1-3 years ahead) over Sen slope continuation, Sen if Mann-Kendall significant, own AR(1), own average, last value, all-years level + trend.
band_app: 68%, symmetric (average of empirical lower/upper backtest deviations), clipped to 0-100
not_projected_values: No projection or placeholder is exported for these counties.

strict_validation.design: CRI rebuilt at each origin from raw SAIDI/SAIFI using only data <= origin; level window chosen on targets <= 2020; final test on origins 2020-2024 (targets 2021-2025), never used for selection.

disclosures: Method choice: projections combine each county's own recent level with one national trend. In a strict out-of-time test (2021-2025 targets, no future data) this family had a mean absolute error of 15.2-16.1 CRI points, versus 17.5 for per-county linear trends, 17.7 for per-county Sen's slope and 19.5 for the last observed value.
Window sensitivity: the level window (3, 5, 7 years, all years, or weighted) changes the test error by at most 0.8 points; the 5-year window is used.

Over-projection: in the 2021-2025 test, projections were on average +2.4 CRI points above observed values, because the national trend slowed (from 1.56 points/yr at the 2020 origin to 1.08 at the 2024 origin).

Regional accuracy: the West is least predictable (test error 18.0 points vs 14.4-15.1 elsewhere; 3-year 68% band covered 64% of Western outcomes vs 72-76% elsewhere). Region-specific trends were tested and did not improve accuracy.
Band: the 68% band covered 73-76% of outcomes in the strict test (slightly conservative).

Latest-year coverage: 15 counties with 2024 data have no 2025 value (11 because their reporting utility filed no 2025 reliability data with EIA; 4 because the reporting utility did not list the county in its 2025 service territory). They are still projected from their recent years and show no 2025 value on the map.
Population weights: ACS 5-year vintages used by year: 2025->2024 (the ACS 5-year release for a newer year was not yet available).

Scope: the projection is a statistical reliability-risk index (relative to 2013-2025 county-years), not a prediction of actual outages, available capacity, or outage probability at a specific site. It cannot anticipate individual storms, utility investments or other events that change a county's trajectory.

ceiling.meaning: CRI 100 = worse than every U.S. county-year observed 2013-2025. Raw projections above 100 are exported as 100 with Capped_At_100 = True and shown as "99+".

app_display.map: Continuous CRI 0-100, fixed range for all years 2013-2028, OrRd sequential scale (light = most reliable, dark red = least reliable). No discrete-tier toggle. Observed years: CRI; projected years 2026-2028: Projected_CRI, map labelled "Projected". Optional: mark tier_edges_cri on the colour bar.

popup_projected_years: Headline = Popup_Headline (risk level first, then the likely range)
Chance of High or Very High = P_High_or_VeryHigh
app_display.county_search: Selecting a county from search opens the same popup/detail panel as clicking it.
app_display.chart_caption: The likely range is wide from the first projected year because a county's reliability varies a lot from year to year, including major-event outages such as storms. It widens only slightly over time because a bad year does not carry into the next.

fips_note: Zero-padded 5-char strings. Connecticut uses 2022+ planning-region FIPS (09110, 09130, 09140, 09150, 09160, 09180, 09190); 09120 and 09170 have no CRI.
